div.head: II Eg 1.1
div.ab: ⁊ man agífe ælce teoðunge to þam ealdan mynstre, þe seo hernes tohyrð; ⁊ þæt sy þonne swa gelæst, ægðer ge of þegnes inlande ge of geneatlande, swa swa his sulh gega.
⁊ man agife ælce teoþunga to þam ealdan mynstrum, þe seo hyrnes tohyrð; ⁊ þæt sy þonne swa gelæst, ægþer ge of ðegnes inlande ge of geneatlande, swa hit seo sulh gegange.
⁊ man agife ælce teoðunga to ðam ealdum mynstrum, þe seo hyrnes tohyrð; ⁊ þæt sy þonne swa gelæst, ægðer ge of ðegnes inlande ge of neatlande, swa hit seo sulh gegange.
Et reddatur omnis decimatio ad matrem ecclesiam, cui parochia adiacet, de terra tainorum et uillanorum, sicut aratrum peragrabit.
⁊ man agife ælce teoðunga to ðam ealdum mynstrum þe seo hyrnes tohyrð; ⁊ þæt sy þonne swa gelæst, ægðer ge of ðegnes inlande ge of neatlande, swa hit seo sulh gegange.
And man agife ælce teoðunge to þam ealdan mynstre þe seo hernes tohyrð; and þæt sy þonne swa gelæst, ægðer ge of þegnes inlande ge of geneatlande, swa swa hit seo sulh gega.

Und jeder Zehnt werde an die alte Kirche, welcher die Pfarrgewalt zugehört, gegeben; und dies werde dann, sowohl vom unverliehenen [Domanial]boden des Adligen, wie vom Boden [seiner] Hintersassen, entrichtet, so wie der Pflug es überschreitet.
And let every tithe be given to the old minster to which the parish belongs; and let it then be paid thus, both from the thegn's demesne land and from his tenants' land, as the plough passes over it.
And all tithes shall be paid to the old churches to which obedience is due; and payment shall be made both from the thegn's demesne land and the land held by his tenants—all that is under the plough.

And all payment of tithe is to be made to the old minster, to which the parish belongs, and it is to be rendered both from the thegn’s demesne land and from the land of his tenants according as it is brought under the plough.

And each tithe is to be rendered to the old minster to which obedience is due; and that the render must come both from the thane’s personal land and the land let out for rent, whatever is under the plow.

note.label: reprises
note.quote: In VIII Atr 5:1 = I Cn 3:2, he reprised Edgar's distinction between 'headminsters', 'lesser' churches with a cemetery and 'field-churches'.

note.label: substitutes
note.quote: the fuller II Eg 1:1 then substituted for I Cn 11:2

div.note: Liebermann would read ‘hit seo’ for G's ‘his’ (with A and D). Instituta Cnuti I 12c has a parallel Latin version.
swa swa hit seo: swa his G1
old minster: That is, the traditional mother church at the center of a community rather than the newer parish or satellite churches founded afterward.

note.seg: Inst scheint irrig Plural zu verstehen; -a kann Acc. sg. sein
Inst seems wrongly to take this as a plural; -a can be acc. sg.

Nicht die Kathedrale, obwohl diese in älterer Zeit, z. B. 1080 im Konzil zu Lillebonne, bisweilen ‘Mutterkirche’ heisst, sondern (wie Selden Hist. of tithes 264 richtig verstand) die Pfarre (vgl. Gl Kirchenrang 3b) laut 3, 1; unter Æthelred VIII 5, 1 und Cnut I 3, 2 steht sie regelmässig der Stiftskirche gleich; vgl. Taranger Angelsaks. Kirk. 254

Not the cathedral, although in earlier times, e.g. in 1080 at the Council of Lillebonne, this is sometimes called ‘mother church’, but rather (as Selden Hist. of tithes 264 rightly understood) the parish church (cf. Gl Kirchenrang 3b), according to 3, 1; under Æthelred VIII 5, 1 and Cnut I 3, 2 it is regularly placed on a level with the collegiate church; cf. Taranger Angelsaks. Kirk. 254
Der Plural in Rec. II ist unoriginal. Auch VII Atr 4, 1, der dies benutzt, hat Sing.
The plural in Rec. II is not original. VII Atr 4, 1, which uses this passage, also has the sing.
IV Eg 1, 4, dies zitierend, setzt dafür teolunga von earm ge cadig.—‘Thegn’ (s. d. Gl 8c) braucht hier nur noch einen Vollfreien auf grösserem Landgut zu bedeuten
IV Eg 1, 4, quoting this, substitutes teolunga of earm ge cadig. — ‘Thegn’ (see that word in Gl 8c) need mean here no more than a fully free man on a fairly large estate

neat für geneat in diesem Sinne fehlt Ags. Wbb.; s. aber netus, nialman im Consuet. Roff. bei Larking Domesday of Kent 33*.—Vgl. Wb: tunesman; in diesem Wort ‘Dörfler’ sieht das Agsä. für villanus des Domesday Maitland Dom. 59.—Persönlich unfrei ist der geneat, tunman, villanus nicht; nur sein Land vertritt nach aussen nicht er, sondern der Gutsherr.—Geneat bildet hier keinen Ggs. zu gebur oder cotsetl (anders Rect 2); vgl. Gl Bauer 1d. e. 4-g

neat for geneat in this sense is lacking in the A.-S. dictionaries; but see netus, nialman in the Consuet. Roff. in Larking Domesday of Kent 33*. — Cf. Wb: tunesman; Maitland Dom. 59 sees in this word, ‘villager’, the A.-S. equivalent of the villanus of Domesday. — The geneat, tunman, villanus is not personally unfree; it is only that his land is represented externally not by him but by the lord of the manor. — Geneat here forms no contrast to gebur or cotsetl (otherwise Rect 2); cf. Gl Bauer 1d. e. 4-g
G's his steht in keiner anderen Hs. noch auch bei den Benutzern VII Atr 4. VIII 7. I Cn 8. Es widerspricht dem regelmässig geltenden Eigentum Mehrerer an Einem Pfluge; s. d. Gl 2a. c

G's his appears in no other MS, nor in the borrowers VII Atr 4. VIII 7. I Cn 8. It contradicts the ownership of a single plough by several persons, which was the regular rule; see that word in Gl 2a. c
Je der zehnte Streifen des Ackerbodens ergibt den Zehnten
Every tenth strip of the arable land makes up the tithe

Liebermann notes that the rendering of tithes had been enjoined by earlier kings under pain of fines (E. and G. 6; I As.) and excommunication (I Edm. 2), but here for the first time it appears as the definite legal duty of every class of freemen. Edgar’s enactments are repeated by his successors, cf. VIII Atr. 7; 8; I Cn. 8, 1 f. etc.

At present the name ‘minster’ is applied to seven cathedrals and large churches in the country (viz. York, Lincoln, Ripon, Beverley, Southwell, Lichfield and Wimborne), and it likewise appears in a good many place-names in the south. Many of these foundations are certainly spoken of as monasteries in early times, though in other cases such evidence is wanting, but this may be due merely to the absence of information.
The reference in this case is taken by Liebermann to be to the parish or mother church (cf. mater ecclesia, Q; mere iglise, Leis Wl. 1, 1). The reference to the mæssepreost in cap. 3, 1 seems to support this view.

geneatland is land occupied by geneatas (free tenants) who are apparently identical with the gafolgeldan of the earlier laws (cf. In. 6, 3; 23, 3). Sometimes this land is called utland as distinguished from inland, i.e. the land kept by the lord of a manor in his own hands.
Cf. VIII Atr. 7; I Cn. 8, 2; and cf. also II As. 16 for the plough as a basis of reckoning.

note.label: minster
note.seg: The Harley and Corpus texts use the plural. “Minster” describes the old parish churches, often served by a community of priests, to distinguish them from later churches built within their parishes.
